data.why: The app's own synthetic demo (Load synthetic demo button, 8-channel/30s/256Hz, seed 42) is the primary example; a small hand-built CSV matching the app's exact schema (channel-name header, numeric rows, declared sampling rate/units) is also provided to exercise the upload path and includes a missing cell, a flat window, a clipping run, and an amplitude exceedance.

goals: Screen an EEG recording for data-quality problems before running further analysis
Load the built-in synthetic demo to see what each quality indicator looks like on recordings with known artifacts
Upload a CSV or EDF recording, correctly declare its sampling rate and units, and inspect per-channel waveforms
Identify channels with flat segments, possible clipping, amplitude exceedances, or missing samples using configurable thresholds
Check for 50/60 Hz line noise contamination via the Welch PSD spectrum view
Export a self-contained HTML quality report and a CSV metrics table to share or archive the inspection

review.summary: The tree follows the README's stated workflow closely: load the demo or a CSV/EDF with declared rate and units, view traces, flag channels with thresholds you can change, check line noise, and export the HTML and CSV report. It does so with clean general and specific wording and screens that hold up when opened. The only real gaps are the EDF path and opening the exported report, and the tree already says it could not do either, so it can be filed as is.
